identity.title: All-contract desktop UI coverage, design and grounded renderer decision

closure_unit.outcome: Reviewed desktop UI design and exact implementation slices cover every original MT across all three WPs without dropping held cases.

materialized_acceptance.text: AC197-1: Enumerate every canonical MT contract in the three named WPs, including newly added records as applicable, and bind required operator/model workflows, original acceptance/proof refs, valid existing coverage and unresolved cases in this MT design_result. Preserve non-UI obligations by linkage.

AC197-2: The distinct expert UI designer supplies professional materially distinct layouts and shared materials/icons/scrollbars/type/spacing. Docked panes touch with shared dividers and no internal desktop gaps. Drafts remain material references only.

AC197-3: The separate nonauthor workflow tester tries representative prototype actions and multi-step flows and records feasibility/consistency/readability plus empty/loading/error/denied/recovery findings separately from real-app acceptance.

AC197-4: Ground Vulkan API/backend selection in current primary technical sources and actual pinned native renderer/input/accessibility/Handpick contracts. Compare supported existing paths before a verified reusable gap, and bind exact owner/API/source-versus-host disposition. A new engine/asset is not required.

AC197-5: Record two-coder disjoint scopes and one writer for shared app/lib/manifest hooks. Preserve front-to-back/dependency/adversarial responsibilities and all original features/runtime cases. Coordinate exact necessary spec/refinement changes in the owning existing contract before dependent adoption.

AC197-6: Design Settings module tabs with feature subtabs OR an equivalent discoverable system tree. Resolve actual module/feature coverage without a new taxonomy. Keep Engine Profiles INSIDE Settings and full profile dispatch/selection/live-authority contracts; bind discoverability, typed persistence and empty/loading/error/denied/recovery flows.

AC197-7: Ground the existing canonical centralized GPU owner/broker and focused typed client contracts across existing/future modules, with memory accountability and no independent per-module device/pool/budget bypass or new monolith. Resolve allocation/budget/pressure/staging/shared-versus-dedicated/inflight/reclaim/shutdown/device-loss/multiwindow/module-attachment ownership and proof boundaries before adoption; do not assume one adapter/API or relocate unrelated CPU/NPU work.

AC197-8: Bind concrete GUI action/navigation/component/error and Vulkan/GPU memory/lifetime event producers to existing internal_diagnostics and standalone Palmistry correlation/retention contracts. Preserve typed mechanical allowlist/no secret or project content. Reuse MT081–096 and canonical watcher proof; planned crash-survival acceptance is genuine separately admitted owned Product proof, not prototype/OS crash or foreign stop. Bind existing stable event/control IDs, real correlation/session and exact target PID/process-birth identity. Normal explicit shutdown requires its actual acknowledgements and owned drain; no later-empty-process proxy.

specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: All Handshake GUI teams and affected GUI work under the three named WP coverage_sources MUST use KUMIHIMO-ASSET-001 (Kumihimo) through its public contract with an actual Vulkan-backed layer. Preserve existing Handpick and every original GUI/GPU/Settings/diagnostic/Palmistry obligation. A name, catalog entry, configuration label or D3D/OpenGL fallback does not prove Vulkan capability or adoption.

When Handshake needs missing reusable GUI logic, extend the declared canonical Kumihimo original source and reusable public capability FIRST; perform focused owning source proof, normal canonical publication and independent exact remote reread before distinct immutable pinned Handshake host adoption. Consume adequate existing capability without compulsory source changes. No host-local workaround, copied private implementation or host-only fork; host-specific policy/adaptation stays in Handshake under HBR-MODULE-LIFECYCLE-004/007/008.

GUI work MUST follow current build rules using small focused crates/modules with independently selectable source/dependency/build/test/artifact closures and focused typed clients, without large aggregate/sink crates. Bind each implementation MT to its actual owning logical module or existing build unit and respect dependency direction and actual project build budgets under HBR-COMPART-001/002 and HBR-MODULE-LIFECYCLE-001. Preserve the conditional applicability of crate-based rebuild accounting; invent no numerical cap, forced crate split, blanket refactor or all-project hold.
